title: The text discusses the recent successes of Kenyan distance runners, who have outperformed their Ethiopian rivals in international championships, marking a significant shift in dominance in the sport. The article highlights the teamwork and strategic approaches of the Kenyan team, particularly focusing on the performance of Paul Kipkoech and defending champion Ngugi. It also touches on the impressive achievements of Djibouti and Tanzanian runners in marathons, showcasing their unexpected prowess despite limited resources. The piece concludes by suggesting that while African runners excel in distance events, they may need more exposure to high-pressure competitions to succeed on the global track stage.
